title: Onboard credit is not the same as money
subtitle: It is a voucher for the line's own shop, and some of it expires while you sleep.

text: Credit keeps your money on the ship. That is the point of it.
sub: A line would rather hand you spend than cut the fare, because credit comes back to it at retail. Useful, but not equivalent to a lower price.

title: Three sources, three sets of rules

items.head: Line promotional credit
items.body: Attached to a campaign, and often tied to a cabin category or a booking window. Read what it excludes.

items.head: Agency credit
items.body: Comes from the advisor's own arrangement, and stacks on top of the line's rather than replacing it.

items.head: Loyalty or shareholder credit
items.body: Small, reliable, and routinely forgotten. It has to be claimed before sailing, not aboard.

points.label: Refundable?
points.value: Unspent credit either returns to you at the end or simply evaporates.

points.label: Per cabin or person?
points.value: The same figure means two different things depending on this line alone.

points.label: What can it buy?
points.value: Some credit excludes the spa, the casino, or pre-booked excursions.

points.label: When does it land?
points.value: Some is spendable before you sail. Some appears only on day one.

quote: I would take a lower fare over credit almost every time. Credit is only a saving if you were going to spend it anyway.

text: Ask for it stacked, then ask whether it is refundable.
sub: Stacked credit from separate pots is real value. A single large figure with restrictions attached is a marketing number. Two questions tell them apart.

title: Send this to the person who handles the booking
body: Usually one of you reads the terms and one of you reads the brochure. This is for the first one.
